report.source_text: On the HPE of the endobronchial biopsy, a malignant epithelial neoplasm was observed. This neoplasm displayed nests and trabeculae of infiltrating tumor cells. However, the overlying respiratory epithelium remained largely unremarkable, with only focal areas of squamous metaplasia. Focal acinar formation with intra-luminal eosinophilic material, as well as cribriforming, was noted. The cells in question were moderately pleomorphic, possessing a high nucleocytoplasmic ratio, fine chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and a moderate amount of amphophilic to vacuolated cytoplasm (suggestive of mucus cells). Focal regions presented nodules of cells with an intermediate appearance (Figures 4-5). Notably, there was no evidence of marked cytological atypia, necrosis, or heightened mitotic activity.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old male presented with hoarseness and dysphagia, and video-laryngoscopy revealed bilateral adductor cord palsy. Initial CT of the neck and thorax showed tracheal luminal narrowing and lung nodules, while MRI brain showed diffuse cerebral atrophy. An esophageal endoscopy and biopsy were negative for malignancy. Subsequent bronchoscopy revealed significant nodular growth in the mid-trachea causing circumferential luminal narrowing. An endobronchial biopsy from this tracheal growth showed a malignant epithelial neoplasm with features consistent with mucoepidermoid carcinoma, leading to a final diagnosis of low-grade MEC.

MRI of the brain was suggestive of diffuse cerebral atrophy.
Bronchoscopy revealed significant nodular growth in the mid-trachea, leading to circumferential luminal narrowing.

Histopathological examination of the endobronchial biopsy showed a malignant epithelial neoplasm with nests and trabeculae of infiltrating tumor cells, focal acinar formation with intra-luminal eosinophilic material, cribriforming, moderately pleomorphic cells, and features suggestive of mucus cells and intermediate cells, without marked atypia, necrosis, or heightened mitotic activity.
Based on these findings, a final diagnosis of low-grade MEC (using the AFIP grading system) was rendered.
